advice: Test one distinct change in the active panel32 path: inside `gemm`, pack each 32-column B panel into a temporary K-major, contiguous layout, then update the panel32 SME loads and panel pointer steps to consume it. Preserve every FP32 value and the existing accumulation order. Keep allocation and packing inside the timed call; retain the general-size fallback and full GEMM ABI. Hypothesis: contiguous B accesses may improve the SME consumer enough to offset packing and allocation costs. This is unverified.
risks: Packing adds a 1 MiB buffer and a full B read/write pass, which may outweigh any consumer benefit. It also changes the active assembly addressing, so bounds, panel transitions, stack/ABI state, and output coverage need careful validation. Do not infer a speedup from isolated load results.
